question.problem:
What is the first term that is less than $1$ in the following geometric sequence?

$$
125,\,75,\,45,\,27,\,…
$$

The first term that is less than $1$ is the
{{field-1}}th term.
question.worked_solution:
The first term of the sequence is ${a}_{1}=125$ and the common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{75}{125}=\frac{3}{5}.
$$

So, the $n$th term of the sequence can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =125{(\frac{3}{5})}^{n-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want the $n$th term to be less than $1.$
Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & <1 \\ 125{(\frac{3}{5})}^{n-1} & <1 \\ {(\frac{3}{5})}^{n-1} & <\frac{1}{125} \\ \operatorname{log}⁡{(\frac{3}{5})}^{n-1} & <\operatorname{log}⁡(0.008) \\ (n-1)\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{3}{5}) & <\operatorname{log}⁡(0.008) \\ n-1 & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.008)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{3}{5})} \\ n & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.008)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{3}{5})}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we reversed the inequality sign when divided by $\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{3}{5})$ because $\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{3}{5})$ is a negative number. 

Estimating the right-hand side using a calculator, we get

$$
\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.008)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{3}{5})}+1≈10.452.
$$

Therefore, the $11$th term is the first term of the sequence that is less than $1.$
